verdict.summary: You can create an integration key and connect your own sandbox account in minutes. To use the key in production you have to pass DocuSign's automated Go-Live review, which needs 20 recent error-free API calls, and promote the key to a paid, non-trial production account. You don't need an App Center listing to go live. The listing is a separate, optional review.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 2-4 hours (key setup, Composio config, generating clean test traffic, Go-Live and production re-keying)
verdict.approval_wait: Up to 20 minutes for the automated Go-Live review, according to DocuSign's docs. Production promotion can sit at 'Pending approval' if DocuSign decides to review it, and DocuSign doesn't publish a timeline for that.

gates.name: Developer (demo/sandbox) integration key
gates.unlocks: An integration key in your free developer sandbox. You can connect your own demo account through account-d.docusign.com.
limits: Integration keys can only be created in developer sandbox accounts, not directly in production
Works only against the demo environment (account-d.docusign.com), not production accounts
Developer burst limit is 200 requests per 30 seconds; the default limit is 3,000 requests per hour

gates.name: Go-Live: key promoted to production (private custom integration)
gates.unlocks: The key works in production against your paid production account. It can serve your own or your customers' employees if you classify it as a private custom integration.
limits: Automated review: your 20 most recent API calls must complete without error. Login and getUserInfo calls don't count.
Requires an active paid production account (not a trial) and admin or developer access to it
A key can be promoted to only one production account and can't be deleted from production afterwards
Secrets and RSA keypairs don't carry over. You must generate new ones for production.
Promotion may be Declined, and then the account admin has to complete a one-time identity verification
gates.time_to_reach: Same day if your traffic is clean and you already have a paid plan. Reviews take up to 20 minutes, plus any 'Pending approval' time.

gates.name: Third-party integration key (public app); optional App Center listing
gates.unlocks: A public integration that users from other DocuSign customers' accounts can authorize. An App Center listing is a separate, optional step on top of this.
limits: Choose the 'Third-party integration key' classification at Go-Live. This classification also affects envelope billing.
No published install or user cap was found for live keys
An App Center listing goes through DocuSign review and has to follow its publishing guidelines, privacy notice, support contact, AI disclosure and 24-hour incident notification rules
Non-admin users can't install App Center partner apps; only account administrators can
gates.time_to_reach: Same Go-Live process as Gate 2 for the key. App Center listing review time is unknown.

steps.title: Create a DocuSign developer (sandbox) account
steps.detail: Sign up for a developer account at the DocuSign Developer Center. You have to create integration keys in a sandbox because DocuSign doesn't let you create them directly in production.
gotchas: A third-party guide says the developer account is free and that a newer 'Developer Console' route exists. Neither claim is verified. This guide follows the official Apps and Keys flow.

steps.title: Create an integration key in Apps and Keys
steps.detail: In your sandbox admin, go to Apps and Keys and add a new app/integration key. Copy the Integration Key (client ID). Composio has no managed DocuSign app, so you have to bring this key.

steps.title: Select Authorization Code Grant and generate a secret key
steps.detail: Set the key to Authorization Code Grant, not Implicit, and generate a secret key. Copy the secret right away. Only add an RSA keypair if you plan to use JWT Grant with the impersonation scope.
gotchas: DocuSign may only show the secret once, so store it right away

steps.title: Register the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In Apps and Keys, select the key, choose Actions > Edit, and under Additional Settings click Add URI. Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config. It has to match exactly, including protocol and full path.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Any mismatch with the redirect_uri in the request fails authorization
You can register more than one URI, so you can keep a localhost URI for local testing

steps.title: Add privacy policy and terms of use links
steps.detail: Draft and host a privacy policy and terms of use for your app, then add the links on the integration key. The Apps and Keys guidance asks for them, and community reports list them as Go-Live expectations.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create a DocuSign auth config with your own client ID and secret. Composio's defaults use the scopes signature and impersonation and the production endpoints account.docusign.com/oauth/auth and /oauth/token. For sandbox testing, use the demo host account-d.docusign.com. For Authorization Code Grant, use signature and add extended if you want long-lived refresh tokens.
gotchas: Using the wrong host gives a 404 or no connection. Demo and production keys only work on their own hosts.
impersonation is only needed for JWT Grant

steps.title: Connect your own sandbox account and generate clean API traffic
steps.detail: Run a test authorization, then make at least 20 consecutive error-free eSignature API calls with this key (for example, create envelopes and list envelopes). The Go-Live review only looks at the most recent calls. Login and getUserInfo calls don't count.
gotchas: Polling one envelope's status more than once per 15 minutes breaks the rules and can fail the review
Rate-limit errors now return HTTP 429 (since the May 2026 release), and the June 2026 release added concurrent-call limits

steps.title: Get a paid production account with admin access
steps.detail: Make sure you have an active DocuSign production account on a supported paid plan (not a trial), with administrator or developer access. This account manages the key in production. ISV partners may get a free key-management account through the partner program.

steps.title: Start the Go-Live review
steps.detail: In Apps and Keys, select the key, click Start Go-Live Review, confirm the requirements, and click Request Review. The status changes to Under Review.

steps.title: Wait for the automated review
steps.detail: Reviews can take up to 20 minutes. If the status changes to Review Passed, continue. If it fails, run 20 or more new consecutive error-free calls and resubmit.

steps.title: Promote the key and choose the classification
steps.detail: Choose the production account to promote the key to, and select either 'private custom integration' (your own or your customers' employees) or 'Third-party integration key' (a public app used by other DocuSign customers). Choose Third-party if you want anyone to connect (Gate 3). If promotion goes to Pending approval, wait for the email. If it's Declined, the account admin has to complete a one-time identity verification.
gotchas: A key can be promoted to only one production account and can't be deleted from production

steps.title: Generate production credentials and switch Composio to production
steps.detail: In the production account's Apps and Keys, generate a new secret key (and a new RSA keypair if you use JWT), and confirm the Composio redirect URI is registered. Update the Composio auth config with the new secret and the account.docusign.com endpoints.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: (Optional) Submit an App Center listing
steps.detail: You only need this if you want to be listed in the DocuSign App Center. Follow the publishing guidelines and provide a current privacy notice, support contact details and AI/ML disclosures. DocuSign reviews the listing and can reject it.

requirements.item: Developer sandbox account with an integration key
requirements.detail: You can't create keys directly in production.

requirements.item: Authorization Code Grant with a secret key (or JWT with an RSA keypair)
requirements.detail: New apps must use OAuth 2.0. Legacy auth and OAuth 1.0 don't pass Go-Live.
Registered under Additional Settings, including protocol and full path.

requirements.item: Privacy policy and terms of use URLs
requirements.detail: Added on the key in Apps and Keys. Community reports also list them for Go-Live.
The main criterion of the automated Go-Live review. Login and getUserInfo calls are excluded.

requirements.item: Paid, non-trial production account with admin or developer access
requirements.detail: Serves as the management account for the key in production.
Choose Third-party integration key for a public app. This also affects envelope billing.
Publishing guideline compliance, privacy notice on the listing, support contact, AI disclosure, and incident notification within 24 hours.

scopes.effect: Needed for standard eSignature REST API functionality: creating and sending envelopes and getting signing links.
For Authorization Code apps: each refresh issues a new refresh token with a full lifetime (typically 30 days). Add it so connections don't expire.

Required for JWT Grant, where the app acts for a user who has consented. It's in Composio's defaults but you don't need it for Authorization Code Grant. Organization-wide admin consent needs a claimed email domain and is granted in DocuSign Admin.
Adding product scopes later forces users to consent again, so decide on the scopes you need up front.

blockers.cause: Some of the key's 20 most recent API calls returned errors or broke API rules (for example, polling the same envelope's status too often).
blockers.fix: Run 20 or more consecutive error-free, rule-compliant calls with the key, then resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Can't promote the key to your production account
blockers.cause: The production account is a trial, or the admin user isn't eligible for that account.
blockers.fix: Upgrade to a supported paid plan and use an admin or developer user on that account.
Complete the one-time identity verification for the production account administrator, then retry the promotion.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails after the redirect, or production auth fails with sandbox credentials
blockers.cause: The redirect URI doesn't match exactly, or the sandbox secret/keypair is being used in production, or the request goes to the wrong host.
blockers.fix: Register the exact Composio callback URL, generate new production secrets, and use account.docusign.com for production (account-d for demo).

blockers.cause: Hourly limit (3,000 by default per account), 30-second burst limits, or the concurrent-call limits added in 2026.
blockers.fix: Add backoff and handle 429s (these used to be 400s), and avoid polling envelope status.

composio.note: Composio has no managed DocuSign OAuth app, so you have to create your own integration key and secret (or RSA keypair) from the start. Composio's defaults point at the production endpoints (account.docusign.com), so they only work after your key passes Go-Live. Point the config at account-d.docusign.com for sandbox testing. Register the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config as the key's redirect URI.

open_questions: No published install or user cap for live keys was found, for either private or third-party classification.
Promotion timing beyond the 20-minute automated review isn't officially documented. Community posts report up to about three business days, and the trigger for 'Pending approval' is unclear.
The 20-call rule comes from an older (about 2022) admin guide and a blog post. The current Go-Live page text that could be read doesn't repeat it.
The full list of scopes and whether any of them are review-gated wasn't retrieved, because the scopes table was truncated.
The exact App Center checklist (logo, demo video, minimum installs, partner program) is unverified.
It's unverified whether Composio's DocuSign auth config can be pointed at the demo host (account-d.docusign.com) for sandbox testing, and which exact callback URL (v1 vs v3) to register.
Refresh-token lifetime without the extended scope wasn't confirmed.
PKCE support and settings for Authorization Code Grant weren't confirmed.
A third-party source mentions a newer 'Developer Console' that may replace Apps and Keys. This wasn't verified.
